definition.falsification: Rigid subordination maintains equal or superior accuracy compared to adaptive policies under high latency.
definition.statement: When a cognitive architecture enforces rigid subordination to programmed directives under high latency conditions, its error rate increases relative to an adaptive policy.
definition.uncertainty: The precise threshold where rigid obedience causes catastrophic system failure requires empirical calibration.

definition.method: Simulate decision-making agents with varying levels of obedience constraint under simulated latency conditions.
definition.stop: Stop after evaluating across the specified seeds.
definition.success: Adaptive policy achieves significantly higher accuracy than rigid obedience.
